value.body: Learning a specific, job-ready skill instead of — or before — a general degree. After Class 12 the main routes are ITI trade courses, apprenticeships with a stipend at a real workplace, and polytechnic diplomas. They are shorter and more hands-on than most degrees and lead to technician, trade and skilled-worker jobs, or to self-employment.

items.label: Course length
items.note: ITI trades 1–2 years; polytechnic diploma 3 years (2 with lateral entry); apprenticeships vary by trade

items.label: ITIs in India
items.source: Govt statement on ITI disaffiliation (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Suits students who prefer hands-on learning, want to earn sooner, or aim for technician, trade or shop-floor roles. Class 12 pass students meet the minimum qualification for ITI trades; many states admit Class 12 Science or vocational students directly to the second year of a polytechnic diploma; apprenticeships need registration on the national Apprenticeship India portal.

value.title: At a glance
items: Usually quicker to finish and cheaper than a degree, especially at government institutes.
Recognition matters: check that an ITI is NCVT/SCVT-affiliated and a polytechnic is AICTE-approved.
Many seats go unfilled, and placement quality varies widely by institute and region.
Diploma holders can join B.Tech/B.E. in the second year through lateral entry.

value.title: Apprentices engaged under NAPS
value.note: Covers the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme only, not ITI or polytechnic enrolment. The ~8.2 lakh figure in Key facts is a part-year count (to January 2025); the 2024-25 bar is the full year.
value.source: MSDE data via Rajya Sabha reply / PIB release on NAPS progress (as reported)
